content.prompt: In the diagram, $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $AB=AC$, $\angle ABC=55^\circ$, $AD\parallel EG\parallel FI$ and $DI\parallel AC$.

spec.description: Isosceles ABC with D onAB, E/F onAC, I onBC. G lies onDF and on the separate segments EG/GI; E,G,I are not collinear.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC, AD parallel EG parallel FI, DI parallel AF. Exact proportional coordinates preserve incidences and parallels. GD=GI and FGI34 are conditional givens in partd; the schematic does not supply measured answers.

answer.worked:
$\angle ACB=55^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$).
$\angle BAC=180^\circ-55^\circ-55^\circ=70^\circ$ (angle sum of a triangle).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $\angle FIC$ and prove that $\triangle FIC$ is isosceles.

answer.short: $\angle FIC=55^\circ$. Since $\angle FIC=\angle FCI$, $\triangle FIC$ is isosceles.
answer.worked:
$\angle FIC=\angle ABC=55^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $FI\parallel AB$).
$\angle FCI=\angle ACB=55^\circ$ because $F$ lies on $AC$ and $I$ lies on $BC$.
Thus $\angle FIC=\angle FCI$, so $FC=FI$ (sides opposite equal angles). Therefore $\triangle FIC$ is isosceles.

$\angle DIB=\angle ACB=55^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $DI\parallel AC$).
$\angle DBI=\angle ABC=55^\circ$ because $D$ lies on $AB$ and $I$ lies on $BC$.
Thus $\angle DIB=\angle DBI$, so their opposite sides are equal: $DB=DI$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: If $GD=GI$ and $\angle FGI=34^\circ$, find $\angle GIF$ and $\angle EFG$.

answer.worked:
$\angle DGI=180^\circ-34^\circ=146^\circ$ (straight angle, $D,G,F$ collinear).
Since $GD=GI$, the base angles of $\triangle DGI$ are equal:
$$\begin{align*}\angle GDI&=\frac{180^\circ-146^\circ}{2}=17^\circ\\\angle DIG&=17^\circ.\end{align*}$$
$\angle DIF=\angle BAC=70^\circ$ (the sides are parallel to $AC$ and $AB$).
$\angle GIF=70^\circ-17^\circ=53^\circ$.
$\angle EFG=\angle GDI=17^\circ$ (alternate angles, $FE\parallel DI$).
